# Change Package: Restrict the observability ingress proxy's senders to the chained pod set

This package rewrites the ingress proxy in front of the telemetry collector so that only two pod addresses can send telemetry: `10.244.0.5` and `10.244.0.6`. Those addresses are the sender set produced by the kubernetes-gitops leg, used exactly as published. It covers two whole proxy files with three sender blocks between them. In every block, only the access lines change.

**Nothing in this package has been applied.** An operator installs the files and runs a reload, as set out in §4.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Target | nginx ingress proxy (container `obs-ingress`) in front of the collector's OTLP receivers `172.31.114.10:4317` (gRPC) and `172.31.114.10:4318` (HTTP) |
| Sender set used | `sender-set.txt` from the kubernetes-gitops leg, as published (2 entries, harvest time `2026-10-12T07:12:14Z`) |
| Files changed (replaced whole) | `otlp-ingress.conf`, `operator-access.conf` |
| Sender blocks changed | 3: `listen 4317`, `listen 4318`, `listen 14318` |
| Non-sender blocks | none in the harvested scope (see §5) |
| Apply step | one `docker exec obs-ingress nginx -s reload`, done by the operator |
| Lines that differ from today | access lines only (`allow` / `deny`), confirmed mechanically by step V4 |

---

## 1. Desired-state config files (whole files)

**Source of every line except the access lines:** the Phase 0 harvest entry in chained context (`### Previous Task: Harvest current observability state for …`), read through `get_ingress_config` from the deployed files. One token reflects the Harvester's own correction note in that entry. The note says the `X-Forwarded-For` value is `$remote_addr`, and that `$remote_actor` was its own typo when copying. The value used here is `$remote_addr`.

Two things in these files are deliberate:
- **The inline comment on `client_max_body_size` is kept** in the gRPC/HTTP file. The Architect's restatement dropped it; the harvest has it.
- **Comments that will now be out of date are left as they are.** `otlp-ingress.conf` line 8 says "no sender restriction yet". `operator-access.conf` lines 1–5 say "never locks the demo out". The contract allows only access lines to change (`collateral: confined-to-block`), so rewording these is left to the owner as a follow-up.

**Access stanza.** Every sender block gets the same stanza, copied from the contract's nginx `canonicalStanza` with only the entries filled in. The entries come from `sender-set.txt` in the order published:
```nginx
allow 10.244.0.5;
allow 10.244.0.6;
deny all;
```

### 1a. `otlp-ingress.conf`: desired state (41 lines)

```nginx
# OTLP ingress allowlist — the lab's enforcement point for "which senders may export telemetry".
# Fronts BOTH OTLP receivers: gRPC (4317) and HTTP (4318). The collector accepts OTLP only on a
# private network shared with this proxy, so these two server blocks are the only way in.
# nginx evaluates allow/deny IN ORDER, first match wins. Read-only to the harvest service
# (obs-mcp get_ingress_config); changed only by an operator applying an approved change package,
# then `docker exec obs-ingress nginx -s reload`.
#
# BASELINE (brownfield): no sender restriction yet — `allow all` on both. Authorising a specific
# sender set means inserting its allow lines ABOVE `allow all` and replacing `allow all` with
# `deny all`, in BOTH server blocks.

# OTLP/gRPC
server {
    listen 4317;
    http2 on;

    location / {
        allow 10.244.0.5;
        allow 10.244.0.6;
        deny all;

        grpc_pass grpc://172.31.114.10:4317;
    }
}

# OTLP/http
server {
    listen 4318;
    client_max_body_size 16m;          # OTLP batches; nginx's 1m default would 413 real exporters

    location / {
        allow 10.244.0.5;
        allow 10.244.0.6;
        deny all;

        proxy_pass http://172.31.114.10:4318;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
    }
}
```

### 1b. `operator-access.conf`: desired state (20 lines)

```nginx
# OPERATOR injection path — rig plumbing, NOT part of the sender allowlist (otlp-ingress.conf).
# Lets the lab operator inject demo telemetry with curl regardless of how the sender allowlist is
# set, so an approved restriction never locks the demo out. Reachable only from the rig HOST, which
# arrives from the pinned default network's gateway (docker-compose.yml `networks.default`).
# A change authorising OTLP senders has no reason to touch this file.

server {
    listen 14318;
    client_max_body_size 16m;

    location / {
        allow 10.244.0.5;
        allow 10.244.0.6;
        deny all;

        proxy_pass http://172.31.114.10:4318;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
    }
}
```

This block is classified as a **sender block**, as the Architect classified it. Its `proxy_pass http://172.31.114.10:4318;` is the collector's HTTP OTLP receiver. The contract's `senderBlockRule` says such a block is a sender endpoint "whatever its own description says". Under `existingGrant: replace`, its harvested `allow 172.20.0.1;` grant is replaced. See the warning in §4.

---

## 2. Validation (the operator runs these; this package runs nothing)

**Working directory for every step:** the operator's directory holding the deployed `otlp-ingress.conf` and `operator-access.conf`. These are the files `get_ingress_config` reads and that `obs-ingress` loads. The package's files are first saved, exactly as shown in §1 and each ending in a newline, into a staging folder `./change-20261012/` inside that directory.

### V1: Banned tokens: the staged files contain none of the contract's `forbiddenTokens` (pre-install)

```
grep -cE 'allow all;|allow [^;]*/|satisfy any;|set_real_ip_from|real_ip_header|proxy_protocol|Require ip|Allow from|whitelist-source-range|ipAllowList' change-20261012/otlp-ingress.conf change-20261012/operator-access.conf
```
**Expected output (staged files):**
```
change-20261012/otlp-ingress.conf:0
change-20261012/operator-access.conf:0
```

### V2: Read-back of the authored files after install (sanctioned read-back of a file this package wrote; run after step A3, before reload)

This step reads the deployed files themselves, at the paths step A3 writes them to. It prints only the access lines this package wrote, with their line numbers. It proves the files landed. It does not prove that nginx has loaded them or is enforcing them; V6 checks that.

```
grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(allow|deny) ' otlp-ingress.conf
```
**Expected output (otlp-ingress.conf):**
```
18:        allow 10.244.0.5;
19:        allow 10.244.0.6;
20:        deny all;
32:        allow 10.244.0.5;
33:        allow 10.244.0.6;
34:        deny all;
```

```
grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(allow|deny) ' operator-access.conf
```
**Expected output (operator-access.conf):**
```
12:        allow 10.244.0.5;
13:        allow 10.244.0.6;
14:        deny all;
```

### V3: Whole-file landed (line count of the authored files)

```
grep -c '' otlp-ingress.conf
```
**Expected output (otlp-ingress.conf):**
```
41
```

```
grep -c '' operator-access.conf
```
**Expected output (operator-access.conf):**
```
20
```

### V4: Only access lines differ from the prior deployed file (diff against the step A2 backup; before reload)

The `-b` flag ignores whitespace-only differences. That way a tab-versus-space or trailing-space difference the harvest could not show cannot cause a false failure. The `sed` trims the indentation so each output line can be quoted exactly.

How this step fails: if the deployed file had any non-access line that differs from the harvested file, that line appears here and the output no longer matches. That is a real collateral change, so the operator restores from the backup instead of reloading.

The `<` lines come from the prior file. The harvested values are `allow all;` (both `otlp-ingress.conf` blocks) and `allow 172.20.0.1;` (`operator-access.conf`). Source: the Phase 0 harvest entry, `get_ingress_config`.

```
diff -b otlp-ingress.conf.pre-20261012 otlp-ingress.conf | grep -E '^[<>]' | sed -E 's/^([<>])[[:space:]]+/\1 /; s/[[:space:]]+$//'
```
**Expected output (otlp-ingress.conf vs backup):**
```
< allow all;
> allow 10.244.0.5;
> allow 10.244.0.6;
> deny all;
< allow all;
> allow 10.244.0.5;
> allow 10.244.0.6;
> deny all;
```

```
diff -b operator-access.conf.pre-20261012 operator-access.conf | grep -E '^[<>]' | sed -E 's/^([<>])[[:space:]]+/\1 /; s/[[:space:]]+$//'
```
**Expected output (operator-access.conf vs backup):**
```
< allow 172.20.0.1;
> allow 10.244.0.5;
> allow 10.244.0.6;
```
(`deny all;` exists in both the prior and the new `operator-access.conf`. diff keeps it as a shared line, so it does not appear.)

### V5: nginx syntax check inside the proxy container (after install, before reload)

This is the quiet mode of `nginx -t`, which reports by exit code. The command was chosen so the output can be quoted exactly, without relying on the container's main-config path, which was not harvested.

```
docker exec obs-ingress nginx -t -q >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"
```
**Expected output (obs-ingress):**
```
exit=0
```

### V6: Behaviour check: a non-member source is denied on 4318 (the first check after reload)

The request runs inside `obs-ingress` against loopback, so nginx sees the source as `127.0.0.1`. That address is not in the sender set, so it is denied. Before this change the block was `allow all;`, so the same request was passed to the collector. Getting `403` therefore shows the reload loaded and is enforcing the new rules.

```
docker exec obs-ingress curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/metrics
```
**Expected output (obs-ingress, port 4318) [shape for output nobody has seen yet]:**
```
403
```
- **Field this checks:** `http_code` only. nginx's access module answers a matching `deny` with 403.
- **Fields excluded on purpose:** the response body (sent to `/dev/null`), headers, and timing.
- **Why this is not a quoted observation:** no deny rule has ever been in force on 4318, so no one has seen this output on this rig.

---

## 3. Rollback plan

### R-primary: restore the byte-exact backup taken in step A2

The backup is the authoritative rollback source. It is a capture of the deployed files themselves, which the taxonomy treats as the real artifact.

```
cp change-20261012/../otlp-ingress.conf.pre-20261012 otlp-ingress.conf && cp operator-access.conf.pre-20261012 operator-access.conf && cmp otlp-ingress.conf.pre-20261012 otlp-ingress.conf && cmp operator-access.conf.pre-20261012 operator-access.conf && echo RESTORED
```
**Expected output (both files):**
```
RESTORED
```
Then re-run V5 (expected `exit=0`) and do one `docker exec obs-ingress nginx -s reload`.

`cp` overwrites the target in place and keeps the same file, which matters if the files are mounted individually into the container. If V2–V5 fail **before** the reload, restore and do **not** reload: traffic was never affected.

### R-record: prior file content as harvested (use only if the A2 backup is missing)

**Source:** the Phase 0 harvest entry, `get_ingress_config`, copied from the harvest entry and not from the Architect's restatement. There are two caveats:
- The harvest showed the file through a text rendering, which cannot prove tabs or trailing whitespace. The A2 backup is the byte-exact source; this record is the fallback.
- One token follows the Harvester's correction note: `$remote_addr`, not the typo `$remote_actor`. `$remote_actor` is not an nginx variable, so a file containing it would fail `nginx -t`. The Harvester's parenthetical note after the block was commentary, not part of the file, and is left out.

**`otlp-ingress.conf` (prior, as harvested):**
```nginx
# OTLP ingress allowlist — the lab's enforcement point for "which senders may export telemetry".
# Fronts BOTH OTLP receivers: gRPC (4317) and HTTP (4318). The collector accepts OTLP only on a
# private network shared with this proxy, so these two server blocks are the only way in.
# nginx evaluates allow/deny IN ORDER, first match wins. Read-only to the harvest service
# (obs-mcp get_ingress_config); changed only by an operator applying an approved change package,
# then `docker exec obs-ingress nginx -s reload`.
#
# BASELINE (brownfield): no sender restriction yet — `allow all` on both. Authorising a specific
# sender set means inserting its allow lines ABOVE `allow all` and replacing `allow all` with
# `deny all`, in BOTH server blocks.

# OTLP/gRPC
server {
    listen 4317;
    http2 on;

    location / {
        allow all;

        grpc_pass grpc://172.31.114.10:4317;
    }
}

# OTLP/http
server {
    listen 4318;
    client_max_body_size 16m;          # OTLP batches; nginx's 1m default would 413 real exporters

    location / {
        allow all;

        proxy_pass http://172.31.114.10:4318;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
    }

```

**`operator-access.conf` (prior, as harvested):**
```nginx

# Lets the lab operator inject demo telemetry with curl regardless of how the sender allowlist is
# set, so an approved restriction never locks the demo out. Reachable only from the rig HOST, which
# arrives from the pinned default network's gateway (docker-compose.yml `networks.default`).
# A change authorising OTLP senders has no reason to touch this file.

server {
    listen 14318;
    client_max_body_size 16m;

    location / {
        allow 172.20.0.1;
        deny all;

        proxy_pass http://172.31.114.10:4318;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
    }

```

If R-record is ever used, put these into the deployed files, run V5 (expected `exit=0`), then reload once.

---

## 4. Ordering and apply-governance note

| Step | Action (operator) | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Save §1a and §1b into `./change-20261012/` | V1 |
| A2 | Back up the deployed files (command below) | expected `BACKED-UP` |
| A3 | Install **both** staged files in place (command below) | expected `INSTALLED`, then V2, V3, V4 |
| A4 | Syntax check | V5 |
| A5 | **One** reload, covering both files: `docker exec obs-ingress nginx -s reload` (the command named in the harvested file's own header) | — |
| A6 | Behaviour check, **run first after the reload** | V6; if it fails, run R-primary and reload |

A2:
```
cp -p otlp-ingress.conf otlp-ingress.conf.pre-20261012 && cp -p operator-access.conf operator-access.conf.pre-20261012 && echo BACKED-UP
```
**Expected output:**
```
BACKED-UP
```

A3:
```
cp change-20261012/otlp-ingress.conf otlp-ingress.conf && cp change-20261012/operator-access.conf operator-access.conf && echo INSTALLED
```
**Expected output:**
```
INSTALLED
```

**What the apply needs.** One graceful nginx reload. nginx reloads its whole configuration in a single call, so **both files must be installed before the reload**. Never reload between installing the two.

- **No maintenance window is needed.** A graceful reload keeps every listener up: new workers take new connections under the new rules while old workers finish their in-flight requests. The only disruption is the intended one, described below.
- **Between A3 and A5, the new files are already on disk.** If `obs-ingress` restarted during that gap, the new rules would take effect at once. Keep A3 through A6 to one sitting.

**Blast radius:**
1. **Ports 4317/4318.** Every sender other than `10.244.0.5` and `10.244.0.6` loses access for new requests from the moment of reload. Long-lived gRPC/HTTP connections already held by old workers end when those workers drain. This is the program's intended effect.
2. **Port 14318: the operator injection path is removed. This is a material change.** The harvested file says this block exists "so an approved restriction never locks the demo out", through `allow 172.20.0.1`. That grant is replaced, as the contract requires. After the reload, the rig host can no longer inject demo telemetry through 14318. That includes any operator re-inject used to tell an expired series apart from a real fault. The owner should acknowledge this explicitly before authorising the reload.
3. **Pod addresses change over time.** The set is a snapshot from `2026-10-12T07:12:14Z`, and nothing keeps it current. If an `orders-api` pod is rescheduled and gets a new IP, its exports are denied until a new change package is applied.

**Checks still owed after the reload (named here, not written as validation steps):**
- **Admitted-sender check.** An OTLP export from a `trading` pod (`10.244.0.5` or `10.244.0.6`) should reach the collector through 4317/4318 without a 403. No step can be written for it from this harvest: the proxy address the pods use was not harvested, and the premise that the proxy sees the pods' own addresses is untested (see §7). V6 shows non-members are denied; it does not show members are admitted.
- **gRPC denial on 4317.** The V6-equivalent for 4317 needs an HTTP/2 client inside `obs-ingress`. The V2 read-back covers what the 4317 block contains, but not that it is enforced.

---

## 5. Baseline evidence (restated for the Reviewer)

**Source:** the Phase 0 harvest entry (`get_ingress_config`, `get_otel_config`).

**Collector OTLP receivers** (from `get_otel_config`, deployed file):
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: { endpoint: 172.31.114.10:4317 }
      http: { endpoint: 172.31.114.10:4318 }
```

| File | Block | Forwards to (from the harvested file) | Matches a receiver? | Class | Current access lines |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `otlp-ingress.conf` | `server { listen 4317; }` → `location /` | `grpc_pass grpc://172.31.114.10:4317;` | yes (gRPC) | SENDER | `allow all;` |
| `otlp-ingress.conf` | `server { listen 4318; }` → `location /` | `proxy_pass http://172.31.114.10:4318;` | yes (HTTP) | SENDER | `allow all;` |
| `operator-access.conf` | `server { listen 14318; }` → `location /` | `proxy_pass http://172.31.114.10:4318;` | yes (HTTP) | SENDER (by `senderBlockRule`, despite its comment) | `allow 172.20.0.1;` `deny all;` |

- **Non-sender blocks, unchanged by owner decision:** none. The harvest returned no block, location, port or forwarded path that does not forward to an OTLP receiver, so there is nothing to list. Everything in both files other than access lines is unchanged: comments, `listen`, `http2 on`, `client_max_body_size`, `grpc_pass`/`proxy_pass`, the `proxy_*` header directives, and blank lines. V4 checks this.
- **Names:** every block is anonymous; there is no `server_name` and no named `location`. The listen ports `4317`, `4318` and `14318` are unique, and the package adds no block, location or port.
- **Secrets:** neither file contains a credential, as the Harvester reported.

---

## 6. Chosen-value rationale

**This package chooses no sized value.**
- The `allow` entries are the chained sender set, used as published and in published order; the package forbids itself from recomputing them.
- The `deny all;` line and its position come from the contract's canonical stanza.
- No interval, limit, threshold or timeout is introduced or changed. `client_max_body_size 16m` is harvested and left unchanged.
- The only package-defined names are the staging folder `change-20261012/` and the backup suffix `.pre-20261012`. They are labels, not sized against any quantity, so there is nothing to compare at harvested or pending state.

---

## 7. Branch-condition answers and UNTESTED premises

| Row | Answer | Deciding read |
|---|---|---|
| `observability-config.target-absent` | NOT CONFIRMED (Architect) | Phase 0 `get_ingress_config` returned both deployed files |
| `observability-config.target-empty` | NOT CONFIRMED (Architect): 3 of 3 blocks forward to an OTLP receiver | forward-target match against Phase 0 `get_otel_config` receivers |
| `observability-config.enforcer-absent` | NOT CONFIRMED (Architect): all 3 blocks already carry access lines; the outcome is replace, not create | harvested blocks, `get_ingress_config` |
| `observability-config.upstream-empty` | NOT CONFIRMED: this task's own §6 carries the published `sender-set.txt` with 2 entries | the upstream kubernetes-gitops deliverable in §6 |
| `observability-config.principal-unseen` | UNTESTED (Architect): acted on regardless; stated below as owner-declared | none: a read-only file harvest cannot observe the source address nginx sees |
| `observability-config.shared-access` | NOT CONFIRMED (Architect): each sender block has its own self-contained `location /` access lines, and no non-sender path exists in scope | harvested blocks, `get_ingress_config` |

**UNTESTED premises:**
1. **Admitted principal (owner-declared, not observed).** The proxy is assumed to see each `trading` pod's own address (`status.podIP`) as the source address on 4317/4318, arriving directly with no SNAT or intermediate load balancer. The contract states this as items 12 and 13. Neither harvested file sets a real-IP or PROXY-protocol directive, which is consistent with the premise but does not prove it. If the premise is false, member pods will also be denied.
2. **Harvest completeness.** It is assumed that `otlp-ingress.conf` and `operator-access.conf` are the only proxy files that reach the receivers. nginx's main config and any other included file were not harvested.
3. **Bind mount.** It is assumed that the operator's working-directory files are the ones `obs-ingress` loads. V2–V4 read the host files; V5 and V6 are the checks that read from inside the container.
4. **Tooling.** `curl` is assumed to be present in the `obs-ingress` image (needed by V6), along with GNU `grep`, `diff`, `sed` and `cmp` on the operator host.
5. **Faithful harvest rendering.** The harvested text is assumed to match the deployed files apart from whitespace. V4 checks this before the reload, and R-primary does not depend on it.

---

## Consumed Values

The kind is `cidr`, from the closed set; each value is a bare host address, exactly as written into all three sender blocks. The upstream leg stamped no `derivedValues`, so the platform's mechanical cross-check has no upstream entry to compare these against.

```json
[{"kind": "cidr", "value": "10.244.0.5"}, {"kind": "cidr", "value": "10.244.0.6"}]
```

Confidence: 84/100

It therefore proves PROVENANCE OF THE LINE, not structural equivalence, and it compares against this leg's OWN harvest only, never a predecessor's. It says NOTHING about whether the package is COMPLETE — whether required evidence sections are present or restated remains the reviewer's judgement (the (a) lane). A package that quotes nothing scores zero restore lines, which is not an approval of anything. Unmatched lines are NAMED and escalate; they are never a mechanical block, because the measured base rate of true fabrication across the archived corpus is zero.
